client.name: Tidewell Physio
client.description: A network of 14 physiotherapy clinics. Patients book a course of 6–10 sessions; revenue depends on patients completing the course.

engagement.goal: Reduce missed appointments and mid-course drop-off without adding front-desk headcount.
constraints: Must integrate with the existing ClinicDesk booking system (read/write API available)
No new front-desk hires in this financial year
Patient messaging must meet UK GDPR and NHS data-handling guidance

items.source: ClinicDesk booking export, all 14 clinics, Jan–Jun
items.summary: 18.4% of booked appointments were missed without notice (no-show), across 41,200 appointments. Rate is consistent across clinics (range 15–22%).
34% of patients who start a course stop before session 4. Of those, 71% had at least one no-show before dropping off.

items.source: SMS reminder pilot, 3 clinics, 6 weeks, randomized by appointment
items.summary: A 24-hour SMS reminder with a one-tap reschedule link cut no-shows from 18.9% (control, n=2,310) to 9.7% (treatment, n=2,284). Difference significant at p<0.01.
38% of patients who tapped the reschedule link rebooked within the same week, filling slots that would otherwise have been lost.

items.source: 12 interviews with patients who dropped off mid-course
items.summary: 9 of 12 said they stopped because they 'felt better' or 'didn't see the point of the remaining sessions'; none had been told what the full course was meant to achieve.

items.source: 8 interviews with front-desk staff across 5 clinics
items.summary: Front desk spends roughly 90 minutes per day phoning patients to confirm appointments. Staff consistently name this as the task they would most like removed.

items.source: ClinicDesk API review with Tidewell IT
items.summary: ClinicDesk exposes appointment read/write and webhook events for booking changes. Rate limits (600 req/min) are well above projected load.

items.source: Moderated test of reschedule flow, 10 patients aged 25–78
items.summary: 10 of 10 completed the reschedule flow from SMS; median time 41 seconds. Two participants over 70 hesitated at the date picker but completed it.
Clinical leads agree that a short 'why your course matters' message after session 1 is clinically appropriate and want to approve the wording.
61% of respondents said they would prefer to receive exercise reminders between sessions by SMS; 22% preferred email; 17% wanted none.

items.source: Published studies on physiotherapy adherence (3 papers)
items.summary: Studies associate structured home-exercise reminders with 10–20% better course completion, though settings and populations differ from Tidewell's.

items.source: Finance model built with Tidewell finance lead
items.summary: Each recovered appointment is worth roughly £48 in revenue. At the pilot's effect size, network-wide reminders would recover about 7,900 appointments per year.
